title: Lags before the solve

blocks.text: A water utility's planners write their dependency rules in whatever words come to hand: "R7 starts two years after R3 starts", "R9 starts a year after R4 is finished", "R5 must be finished no earlier than R2 is finished". Before any row is written, every rule is turned into one start-to-start lag $`L`$, meaning the child may start in year $`t`$ only if the parent started in some year $`s \le t - L`$. A renewal of duration $`d`$ started in year $`s`$ finishes at $`s + d`$.

items: `start_to_start(kind, lag, parent_duration, child_duration)` returns $`L`$ for a lag measured between the two events `kind` names: `"SS"` (parent's start to child's start), `"FS"` (parent's finish to child's start), `"FF"` (parent's finish to child's finish) or `"SF"` (parent's start to child's finish). The child's event must come at least `lag` years after the parent's. $`L`$ may be negative.

`usable_child_years(parent_starts, child_starts, lag)` returns, in increasing order, the child's start years that at least one of the parent's start years serves, for a start-to-start `lag`. The others can be deleted from the model before it is built.

blocks.text: Write each conversion as an inequality between the two events first, then solve it for the child's start. The tests use their own numbers. About ten lines in total.

from __future__ import annotations


def start_to_start(kind: str, lag: int, parent_duration: int, child_duration: int) -> int:
    """The same rule as a start-to-start lag L: the child may start in year t only if t >= parent start + L.

    kind names the two events the lag is measured between: "SS" (start to start), "FS" (parent's
    finish to child's start), "FF" (finish to finish) or "SF" (parent's start to child's finish).
    A project of duration d started in year s finishes at s + d.
    """
    # TODO: convert each kind of lag to start-to-start.
    return lag


def usable_child_years(parent_starts: tuple[int, ...], child_starts: tuple[int, ...], lag: int) -> list[int]:
    """The child's start years that at least one parent start serves (s <= t - lag), in order."""
    # TODO: keep only the child years some parent start can serve.
    return list(child_starts)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(start_to_start("FS", 1, 3, 2), usable_child_years((2027,), (2027, 2028, 2030, 2031), 2))

cases.says: a finish-to-start lag becomes start-to-start by adding the parent's duration, and a start-to-start lag stays as it is
a child year that no parent start can serve is removed from the window
a finish-to-finish lag adds the parent's duration and subtracts the child's
a start-to-finish lag subtracts the child's duration
with a lag of zero the child may start in the parent's start year
a child year is kept when any one of the parent's possible start years serves it
